title: Why I Built an AI Essay Correction App for Taiwanese Learners
excerpt: Aside from it is a requirement for my degree, I built this app to help Taiwanese learners improve their writingskills using AI.
contentHtml:
A Vision for Bilingual 2030, Not Just Perfect Grammar

Taiwan’s Bilingual 2030 goal inspired me, but what I see every day in classrooms tells a quieter story. Many Taiwanese learners want to write well in English, but they struggle not just with grammar; they struggle with confidence. They worry about making mistakes, so they hold back their ideas. As a teacher and researcher, I’ve always wished I could give feedback that is gentle and gradual, one that doesn’t erase the learner’s original voice. I wanted to create a tool that helps them grow, not depend, to make feedback that sticks, not just corrections that impress.

In my lab, we’ve explored existing tools like ChatGPT and Grammarly, but both fall short for learning. ChatGPT is non-deterministic; the same essay can get different answers every time, while Grammarly tends to rewrite too much, lifting learners’ sentences far above their actual level. The result looks perfect, but the student learns nothing. I envisioned something more human: a model that edits like a teacher, not a ghostwriter. It should understand the learner’s level and revise within that level, guiding, not overwhelming. My current prototype lets users input essays, view AI corrections, and soon teachers will be able to edit those outputs to provide tailored guidance. Some suggestions even include showing feedback in tables or bilingual notes, but I plan to validate these through user interviews and A/B testing to see what truly helps learners improve.

My goal isn’t to build an app that students rely on forever; it’s to build one that eventually makes itself unnecessary. I want learners to write with more awareness each time they use it, to internalize the patterns and explanations until they no longer need AI help. In this age of rapid automation, we need to design tools that keep humans thinking, not tools that do all the thinking for them. For me, this project is about creating AI that nurtures curiosity and independence, an app that helps learners learn, not just write better sentences.

title: My Journey Searching for an AI Job in Taiwan
excerpt: I’m navigating my AI job search in Taiwan with patience and determination, learning from every interview and staying hopeful about finding the right opportunity.
contentHtml: My Journey Searching for an AI Job in Taiwan

When I began my job search in Taiwan, I knew I wanted to grow in AI and NLP, ideally in Taipei—but I kept my mind open to starting anywhere that would let me learn fast and contribute meaningfully. What followed has been a steady, reflective journey shaped by interviews, kind rejections, and a lot of perseverance.

I’ve been applying broadly—NLP, AI Engineer, and Deep Learning Engineer roles—because I value hands-on problem solving and I’m eager to join teams where I can help build useful systems. Taipei is my target, but I’m flexible on location to gain the right experience and momentum.

Taiwan’s main job portal, 104.com.tw, is primarily in Mandarin. Even with translation tools, navigating forms and settings has been challenging. Still, hiring managers have tried their best to message me and clarify details, which I appreciate. The administrative friction has taught me to be more patient, organized, and precise in my communication.

Some teams told me they liked my experience but ultimately hired just one person. Even when I wasn’t selected, several sent thoughtful notes about what they appreciated in my profile. Those moments reminded me that every application is an introduction; feedback—accepted or not—is progress.

I’ve noticed care and thoroughness in the Taiwanese hiring process. Decisions can take time, and messages are considerate. I’m learning to write concise, respectful follow-ups, to manage timelines calmly, and to balance persistence with empathy for everyone’s workload.

This search has clarified the environments where I thrive: collaborative teams, clear problem definitions, and space to iterate on real-world AI/NLP challenges. I value candid feedback, documentation, and a culture that pairs curiosity with delivery.

I’ll continue applying to roles where I can contribute to production-grade AI and language technologies, keep improving my Mandarin for smoother collaboration, and refine how I present my projects and research. I’m determined to build a career here in Taiwan—patiently, steadily, and with gratitude for every conversation that brings me closer to the right fit.

I’m still on the journey, but I’m motivated by every interview and every note of encouragement. If my profile aligns with your team’s needs in AI, NLP, or deep learning, I’d love to connect and explore how I can help.
